items.text: NVIDIA is going after the frontier labs (AKA OpenAI, Anthropic) AI infrastructure business directly! Womp, womp hyperscalers. Jensen - "But frontier AI labs are different. Frontier AI labs have extraordinary demand for training and inference compute, but many are growing faster than their balance sheets and long-term credit profiles can support. They may have strong customer demand and rapidly growing revenue yet still lack the decades-long infrastructure contracts and investment-grade financing capacity needed to secure the AI factory infrastructure independently. Their growth is increasingly constrained not by algorithms or customer demand, but by the availability of compute. For these companies, more compute means more intelligence, more products, more users and more revenue. NVIDIA is helping provide the infrastructure that powers this flywheel." OpenAI – "SB Energy will build, own, and operate the data center under a 20-year lease to OpenAI and deliver capacity over time. OpenAI will be the customer and will utilize capacity at the site, which will exclusively host NVIDIA AI compute infrastructure."

items.text: I disagree. Almost every major AI breakthrough out of China has been trained primarily on $NVDA. A free flow of our leading edge GPUs would expedite China’s dominance in AI and models the same way it has in robotics, autonomy, and drones. Policy to slow and/or constrain the flow of leading edge chips as well as WFE/Lithography has slowed China meaningfully. Its recent breakthroughs like Kimi K3 are NVIDIA powered with the support of American frontier models and to China’s credit some meaningful breakthroughs in model delivery. And its GPU/XPU production remains limited without the most advanced tooling. The world’s economic leadership will be decided on AI leadership. China, even if we opened the door to NVIDIA would never have sat idle and became dependent on U.S. innovation, but rather would have had parallel work streams, like it does today. Only we would have made it much easier. The N minus 2 strategy is the best. We can provide 2 generation old American GPUs/Systems to China. Otherwise we are handing global economic leadership to China—Again. 🇺🇸

items.text: Jensen Huang: "Today, we are partnering with SB Energy to secure LPS capacity at the exceptional PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Portsmouth, Ohio, to host NVIDIA compute. OpenAI will be the tenant." "But frontier AI labs are different. Frontier AI labs have extraordinary demand for training and inference compute, but many are growing faster than their balance sheets and long-term credit profiles can support. They may have strong customer demand and rapidly growing revenue yet still lack the decades-long infrastructure contracts and investment-grade financing capacity needed to secure the AI factory infrastructure independently. Their growth is increasingly constrained not by algorithms or customer demand, but by the availability of compute. For these companies, more compute means more intelligence, more products, more users and more revenue. NVIDIA is helping provide the infrastructure that powers this flywheel." "OpenAI will build and operate a world-class AI factory at PORTS-Pike. The AI factory will use NVIDIA’s full-stack DSX AI factory platform, including GPUs, CPUs, networking, and infrastructure software. The initial deployment is expected to provide 4.25 gigawatts of AI factory capacity. Each generation of NVIDIA AI factory systems deployed at PORTS-Pike could represent approximately 1.5 million NVIDIA GPUs, or approximately $150 billion to $200 billion in NVIDIA revenue. Over 20 years, the site can support multiple upgrade cycles. This is the essential economic point: the LPS commitment secures a long-lived AI factory site, while the NVIDIA compute inside can be upgraded repeatedly. Each new generation can deliver greater production, more intelligence and better economics. NVIDIA may also choose to extend the arrangement at PORTS-Pike beyond the initial 4.25 gigawatts to secure the remaining capacity of 3.75 gigawatts." "More broadly, OpenAI has committed to substantial deployments of NVIDIA AI infrastructure through 2030. OpenAI’s existing and planned commitments represent approximately 12 gigawatts of NVIDIA compute, with an opportunity to expand to approximately 16 gigawatts if NVIDIA extends the PORTS-Pike arrangement beyond the initial 4.25 gigawatts. At these levels, the opportunity represents roughly $600 billion of NVIDIA compute through 2030."
